title: Soltés problem for the Kirchhoff index of a graph
summary: We say that $v\in V(G)$ is a \textit{good vertex} if the Kirchhoff index remains unchanged when $v$ is removed, i.e. $Kf(G)=Kf(G-v)$. In 1991, Šoltés studied the Wiener index of a graph and posed the problem of identifying graphs for which the removal of an arbitrary vertex preserves the Wiener index. In this paper, we explore a similar concept: identifying \textit{Kirchhoff Šoltés graphs}, i.e. graphs in which all vertices are good vertices.
